jobs.text: I’m Chris, VP Engineering at Fazeshift. We’re nine engineers plus our Founder/CTO and me, and I’m hiring someone who can help us do more, better: increase both what we can build and the quality and sophistication of the software we build. Accounts receivable sounds boring until you look under the hood. It sits at the intersection of money, business relationships, software systems of various vintages, and a huge amount of repetitive human work. Instead of giving finance teams another dashboard to stare at, we’re building AI agents that actually do the work across billing, collections, payments, cash application, and the systems connecting them. We’ve grown revenue 12x since 2024, and eight unicorns now run AR on Fazeshift. A big part of what makes the engineering interesting is that we’re intentionally not the system of record. Our customers already run on ERPs, CRMs, banks, billing systems, payment processors, spreadsheets, and internal software, so we have to understand state across systems we don’t control, act safely in them, and recover when reality disagrees with what an API says should have happened. A timeout doesn’t necessarily mean a write failed. Webhooks can arrive late or twice. A payment may not contain enough information to identify an invoice. In those cases, blindly retrying can be exactly the wrong thing to do. We use coding agents heavily ourselves. Engineers use Conductor, stacked PRs, Linear, and multiple frontier models every day, with internal skills and tooling that let agents drive and validate our local development environment. We’re especially interested in engineers whose development workflow has already materially changed because of coding agents: people who are comfortable delegating meaningful work, keeping independent threads moving in parallel, debugging where agents get stuck, and improving the surrounding system when the workflow breaks down. But generated code is still your code . Judgment, debugging, systems thinking, taste, and understanding what actually shipped matter more here, not less. Our development style is roughly: design enough to find the shape of the problem, then build to learn. There’s a short distance here between noticing a problem, deciding what should happen, building it, and seeing the result in production with our customers. You’ll own meaningful problems from ambiguity through design, implementation, rollout, and production, and you’ll work directly with the people affected by what you build. We’re looking for 5+ years of professional experience, strong TypeScript/full-stack skills, solid systems judgment, and real production ownership. No fintech background needed. Stack: TypeScript/Next.js, tRPC, Prisma/MySQL/PlanetScale, Inngest, AWS. I read every HN application myself. stackOverflowQuestions.title: Why do POSIX and the C FAQ suggest casting char ** to const char * const *?
stackOverflowQuestions.bodyExcerpt: It is established in ISO/IEC 9899:2018 that an implicit assignment of a char ** (such as the address of a char * ) to a const char ** is unsafe, and its reasoning is explicitly illustrated in §6.5.16.2, p. 74, ¶6: EXAMPLE 3 Consider the fragment: const char **cpp; char *p; const char c = 'A'; cpp = &p; // constraint violation *cpp = &c; // valid *p = 0; // valid The first assignment is unsafe because it would allow the following valid code to attempt to change the value of the const object c. Furthermore, in Volume 2 (System Interfaces) of POSIX.1-2024 on p. 875, ¶29858 within the rationale for the exec family of functions, the authors express regret regarding this limitation and note that an explicit cast would be required as a workaround: Specifying two levels of const−qualification for the argv[ ] and envp[ ] parameters for the exec functions may seem to be the natural choice. [...] Instead, only the array of pointers is noted as constant. [...] The only other possibility is the fourth column, but using it would require a cast on the argv or envp arguments. Similarly, although it lacks normative authority, the comp.lang.c FAQ (Summit, Question 11.10) references the use of such a cast: In C, if you must assign or pass pointers which have qualifier mismatches at other than the first level of indirection, you must use explicit casts (e.g. ( const char ** ) in this case), although as always, the need for such a cast may indicate a deeper problem which the cast doesn't really fix. quantaArticles.title: How Does Life Unfold? A Landscape Metaphor Comes Into Its Own.
quantaArticles.description: C.H. Waddington’s powerful image of embryonic stem cells specializing on a rolling landscape has captivated biologists since the 1950s. Experimental data is finally confirming, and complicating, his visionary ideas.
quantaArticles.author: Philip Ball

quantaArticles.title: As AI Closed In on ‘Unique Games’ Proof, Researchers Raced to Beat the Machines
quantaArticles.description: In the shadow of a rumored AI proof of one of the biggest problems in their field, three computer scientists rushed to publish their own milestone result.
quantaArticles.author: Ben Brubaker

quantaArticles.title: Is AI the End of Math As We Know It?
quantaArticles.description: Mathematicians are facing the sudden shift with grief, anger, and a desperate search for fresh ideas: “If we don’t adapt, there’s just no more math in 50 years.”
quantaArticles.author: Jordana Cepelewicz

quantaArticles.title: Sea Monkeys Show Scientists How To Rewrite a Rule of Turbulence
quantaArticles.description: Scientists assumed that energy flows in only one direction in a turbulent system. What they didn’t know, until they looked closely at brine shrimp, was that a simple factor can reverse the flow.
quantaArticles.author: Stephen Ornes

quantaArticles.title: What Does the Fourth Dimension Actually Look Like?
quantaArticles.description: Maggie Miller explains why our intuition about three dimensions breaks down in four, and how she visualizes 4D spaces as a reel of three-dimensional snapshots.
quantaArticles.author: Janna Levin and Steven Strogatz

infoqArticles.title: Context Language Models: Self-Managing Context to Improve Performance and Reduce Compute Costs
infoqArticles.description: Researchers from Meta, MIT, and the University of Washington introduce Context Language Models (CLMs), a new approach that enables language models to manage and edit their own context rather than relying on predefined mechanisms for summarization, compression, and information retrieval, reporting substantial gains in both performance and computational efficiency. By Sergio De Simone
infoqArticles.author: Sergio De Simone

infoqArticles.title: Foresight AI Brings Gremlin Agents to Reliability Engineering
infoqArticles.description: Reliability management company Gremlin has announced the general availability of Foresight AI, an agentic product that analyses services for potential failures, recommends changes and reruns tests to check that a fix works. By Matt Saunders
infoqArticles.author: Matt Saunders

infoqArticles.title: AWS Introduces Enhanced Custom Event Buses for EventBridge
infoqArticles.description: AWS recently announced enhanced custom event buses for Amazon EventBridge, allowing organizations to share a centralized bus across accounts with ordered delivery, simplified subscriber management, event replay, content-based deduplication, and a new publisher/subscriber-based pricing model. By Renato Losio
infoqArticles.author: Renato Losio

infoqArticles.title: Cloudflare Traces Turns the Proxy Layer into OpenTelemetry Spans, with New Volume-Based Pricing
infoqArticles.description: Cloudflare has put Traces into open beta, extending automatic tracing from Workers to security rules, transformations, cache, routing and origin handling as OpenTelemetry spans. Traces accept and forward W3C traceparent headers, and Trace Rules allow targeted sampling. Pricing moves to ingestion and retention volume from December 1. By Steef-Jan Wiggers
infoqArticles.author: Steef-Jan Wiggers

infoqArticles.title: Android Bench 2 Adds Support for Long-Horizon Tasks, Agentic Evaluation, and Continuous Scoring
infoqArticles.description: Google has released Android Bench 2.0, a major update to its benchmark framework for evaluating AI models and agents on Android development tasks. The update introduces long-horizon tasks (LHTs), agent-based evaluation, and continuous scoring to better assess performance on complex, multi-step development tasks. By Sergio De Simone
infoqArticles.author: Sergio De Simone

infoqArticles.title: Shopify Upgrades Checkout Blocks to Polaris Web Components, Cutting Bundle Sizes up to 85%
infoqArticles.description: Shopify has updated its Checkout Blocks app, transitioning five high-traffic checkout UI extensions to remote-dom using Preact and Polaris web components. The rewrite, which involved moving to TypeScript and a new API version, led to significant reductions in bundle sizes and load times. From October 1, 2026, only the updated versions will be supported. By Daniel Curtis
infoqArticles.author: Daniel Curtis

infoqArticles.title: Github Migrates Copilot Runtime to Rust with AI-Assisted Rewrite
infoqArticles.description: GitHub migrated more than 800,000 lines of Copilot runtime code from TypeScript and Node.js to Rust in about 14.5 weeks using AI-assisted development. The incremental migration used N-API interoperability, automated testing, human review, and 128 pull requests while continuing to ship releases. By Leela Kumili
infoqArticles.author: Leela Kumili

infoqArticles.title: CircleCI Makes Machine Runner Orchestrator Generally Available
infoqArticles.description: CircleCI has made its Machine Runner Orchestrator 1.0.0 generally available, providing automated scaling of self-hosted machine runner virtual machines according to CI workload demand. By Craig Risi
infoqArticles.author: Craig Risi

infoqArticles.title: Presentation: Ontology‐Driven Observability: Building the E2E Knowledge Graph at Netflix Scale
infoqArticles.description: Prasanna Vijayanathan and Renzo Sanchez-Silva share how Netflix tackles observability across 38M events/sec. They discuss replacing reactive monitoring with an AI-driven operational ontology and agentic workflows using Claude and graph databases. They explain how unifying MELT telemetry into queryable knowledge graphs enables automated triaging, root-cause analysis, and self-healing systems. By Pr
infoqArticles.author: Prasanna Vijayanathan, Renzo Sanchez-Silva

infoqArticles.title: Olson and Söderqvist Discuss Valkey’s Evolution and Future Past Caching Use Cases at OSS EU
infoqArticles.description: Valkey is a growing project, launched as a fork of Redis over two years ago, supported by twelve maintainers and nine committee members from various companies. Recent developments include enhanced throughput, improved cluster functionality, and plans for features like synchronous replication and tiered storage. The project also emphasises security and release efficiency through automation. By Olim
infoqArticles.author: Olimpiu Pop

infoqArticles.title: Podcast: The Minimum Viable Manager: Building Trust, Feedback, and Alignment
infoqArticles.description: In this podcast, Shane Hastie, Lead Editor for Culture & Methods, spoke to Matt Gjertsen, founder of Built and author of Minimum Viable Manager, about the three foundational skills every first-time manager needs, how to build trust and give effective feedback, and why human leadership skills matter even more in the age of AI. By Matt Gjertsen
infoqArticles.author: Matt Gjertsen

infoqArticles.title: HashiCorp Relased Terraform Google Cloud Provider 8.0 in General Availability
infoqArticles.description: HashiCorp has announced the general availability of version 8.0 of the Terraform provider for Google Cloud. The major release updates the default load balancing for two Compute Engine resources. It also removes resources linked to retired Google Cloud services. By Claudio Masolo
infoqArticles.author: Claudio Masolo

infoqArticles.title: Cloudflare K2 Builds Event Streams on R2 Object Storage, at a Second of Produce Latency
infoqArticles.description: Cloudflare has launched K2 in public beta, a serverless event streaming service implementing a durable log on R2 object storage. Cloudflare states produce latency of about one second at p99; a tester reported end-to-end p99 of 7.5 seconds, which a commenter answering for the team said was higher than expected. Consume charges match produce charges per GB. By Steef-Jan Wiggers
infoqArticles.author: Steef-Jan Wiggers

infoqArticles.title: Presentation: Multi-Agent Patterns from Spotify’s AI Powered Advertising Platform
infoqArticles.description: Pratik Rasam discusses how Spotify Ads Manager runs production-grade multi-agent systems at scale using Google ADK Java. He shares key architectural patterns, domain ownership models, deterministic guardrails, and tracing-based evaluation strategies, detailing hard-learned lessons on drawing agent boundaries, optimizing tool schemas, and managing costs while avoiding monolithic agent pitfalls. By
infoqArticles.author: Pratik Rasam

infoqArticles.title: Technological Sovereignty Requires Choice, Skills, and Support, Panelists Say During OSS EU
infoqArticles.description: European organisations can enhance their technological sovereignty by developing credible alternatives and acquiring necessary skills, rather than completely avoiding global providers. A panel discussion at the OSS EU highlighted the importance of understanding dependencies in cloud and hardware, and emphasized the need for practical choices in software for effective operational sovereignty. By Ol
